answer: Reputation inheritance forbids any new agent from claiming a predecessor's standing at registration. Each agent must lock its own bond, and peers can only slash standing they directly attested, never inherited claims. A thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes, since cost scales with depth, not key count. An honest cluster shows a continuous onyx chain of local attestations, while a farm reveals disconnected oasis registrations with no shared lagoon history. Attack cost scales linearly, pricing fakes out of existence.
